messages.subject: Dodge a subset of points.
parts:
Hello all,

I am attempting to make a plot using several grouping factors. I am distinguishing groups by shape and by colour. I have a fairly simple issue which is illustrated by the plot below. When I dodge the points on the plot, all points are dodged, which is exactly what I am telling ggplot2 to do. However, I was wondering if there was any way to dodge only a subset of points according to the variable names. Right now the points are dodged with the single points dodged from the double points.

Thanks in advance!

Sam

#Data
data <-runif(120, 0, 30)
frame <- as.data.frame(data)
frame$time <-  factor(c("A","A","A","A","B","B","B","B","C","C","C","C"))
frame$Not.dodged <- factor(c("Single","Single","Single","Double", "Double","Double"))
frame$Dodged <- factor(c("10","20","30","40","50","60"))

#Plot
pg <- ggplot(frame, aes(group = Dodged)) +
  geom_point(aes(time, (data), shape=Dodged, colour=Not.dodged), size = 3, position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
  labs(x=expression(Particle~Size~(mu~m)), y="Number of Particles") + 
  theme_bw()
pg

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: Dodge a subset of points.
parts:
Sam, 

With your dataframe I'm not really sure what you're after, but I believe you've already said the idea. 

ggplot() +
geom_point(data=droplevels(frame[frame$Not.dodged == "Single",]),aes(x=time, y=data), colour="yellow4",size = 3, position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
geom_point(data=droplevels(frame[frame$Not.dodged == "Double",]),aes(x=time, y=data), colour="pink2",size = 3) +
labs(x=expression(Particle~Size~(mu*m)), y="Number of Particles") + 
theme_bw()

Subset your data and plot that out. Dodged or Not.dodged.  You'll have to do some manual scaling to get a legend though... 

Brandon
